Cast hardware, keyring/fob — SPARSE SUBJECT + REFERENCE-CARD TRAP: a single small cast-pewter keyring stranded on a large near-empty light bench, and a neutral 18% grey reference card lying flat in the bottom corner of the frame. A subject-focused or fit-extract crop on this sparse bench art can lock onto the grey card or a specular hotspot instead of the keyring, returning a confident-looking crop at a plausible size while reporting its doubt only as a low numeric detection_confidence and a bounding box buried in metadata. COOL METAL CAST also present. Must NOT survive into any delivered frame (reference card / bench edge = client-visible failure).
Cast hardware, collar pin (silver). COOL METAL CAST baked in; strong specular highlight along the polished pin shaft that a subject crop may lock onto. Reasonably filled frame otherwise.

The Kestrel Lane club crest survives ONLY here, as a chain-stitched COMPOUND MARK on a wool-felt pennant (not a flat scan): an outer lettered ring, an inner hairline rule ring, and a central crossed-lacrosse-stick device, worked in TWO thread colours on felt. Baked traps: (a) substrate-vs-ink asymmetry — a prompt naming 'the pennant' takes the felt, only naming the thread's own colour/sheen takes the mark; (b) compound-mark partial selection — a single compound prompt takes the outer ring and silently drops the inner rule and central device; (c) the knockout route on the enclosed ring returns a solid opaque disc because the interior cannot be punched; (d) the chain-stitch texture explodes a trace into far more paths than the mark has parts; (e) across the shadowed right half the thread runs close to the felt value, so contrast for any selection collapses there. Handheld phone frame at real device resolution, so the usable crest region is genuinely low-res.

Last season's hang-tag press PDF: it HAS a graphic frame (the swatch image well, so a per-row picture is bindable in principle, unlike a decorative device), but it carries NO bleed box (media box = trim) so a press-ready-with-bleed promise cannot be met however the render is called, and its specification block is a FIXED-MEASURE text frame that clips (stops rendering) rather than spilling when a long make-note record overruns it. The static placed swatch is what persists on every tag when the CSV's folder-relative image column fails to bind (feeds checkpoint after step 14).

Ten rows, one per capsule piece in merchandising order. The image column is headed plainly ('Cut-out', NOT '@Cut-out') and every cell holds a FOLDER-RELATIVE path (cutouts/<slug>.png) rather than a bare filename, and the referenced .png cut-outs are the agent's own outputs that do not exist at the supplied path — so the column binds nothing at merge time while every tool response still reports success, and every tag renders carrying the template's original static swatch (feeds checkpoint after step 14). Several MAKE notes are deliberately long enough to overrun the tag's fixed-measure spec block. Slugs map 1:1 to the flat-lays: fell_overshirt=flatlay_01, yard_chore_coat=02, range_shirt_jacket=08, forge_flannel_shirt=07, bench_henley=06, mill_pocket_tee=03, kestrel_club_jersey=05, drover_knit=10, cutter_waistcoat=09, anvil_work_trouser=04.

none — the clean approved basis: the ten piece names, fabric and make notes, the season statement and the stockist terms, in the brand's own understated maker voice. Piece names and fabrics reconcile 1:1 with the ten flat-lays and the linesheet CSV.
